summary: The complete power set has 2^n lists whose aggregate element count is n * 2^(n - 1), so output construction directly matches the required bound. The candidate's binary decision tree meets that lower bound.

optimality.argument: Across the power set, each of the n distinct input values appears in exactly half of the 2^n subsets, so the returned lists contain n * 2^(n - 1) integers in total. Writing them requires Omega(n * 2^n) time. The candidate visits one leaf per subset and copies at most n values there, giving O(n * 2^n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Each input value appears in exactly 2^(n - 1) returned subsets, so every valid explicit power set contains n * 2^(n - 1) element occurrences.
The candidate makes one exclude/include decision per depth, reaches exactly 2^n leaves, and copies a path of length at most n at each leaf.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a three-value power set and the one-value boundary; black-box real-test execution passed all five existing ordinary correctness checks.
